The method / Prove the economics / Step 1
ACTION 13 OF 32 · PHASE 04

Calculate how money actually comes in

Know what you keep from each sale and how many sales you need.

WHEN TO DO THISBefore committing to full build, advertising spend or hiring.ESTIMATED WORK TIME45–90 min
↗
Your one job

Know what you keep from each sale and how many sales you need.

01

Do this now

  1. 01

    List what customers pay, payment fees, shipping/travel, labor, supplies, platform fees, refunds and commissions.

  2. 02

    Calculate contribution margin: revenue per sale minus variable cost per sale.

  3. 03

    Calculate break-even monthly orders: fixed overhead ÷ positive contribution per order.

  4. 04

    Compare best case, likely case and downside case; include capacity and working capital.

02

Copy this into ChatGPT

Replace anything in [square brackets] with your real business details. The prompt is a shortcut, not a substitute for the steps above.

READY-TO-USE PROMPT
Create a business economics worksheet for [PRODUCT/SERVICE] in [COUNTRY]. Inputs are price, variable labor, materials, merchant fees, commissions, freight, returns, fixed overhead and expected monthly capacity. Calculate contribution, gross revenue, operating profit estimate, break-even sales, acquisition cost ceiling and cash-flow risks. Use only values I give you; identify unknowns and scenarios. Include BSD/USD handling where relevant without assuming rates.
03

Finish with this

Unit-economics worksheet with contribution margin, break-even and a cash-survival estimate.

Before moving on, check your work against the following:

  • No cost category silently left at zero
  • Variable contribution is positive or the weakness is explicit
  • Break-even volume fits real capacity
DON’T MAKE THIS MISTAKE

Calling gross sales profit or forgetting fulfillment and partner commissions.

READY TO MOVE ON?

Price exceeds variable costs, capacity and cash needs are realistic, and at least one acquisition path can plausibly work.
